newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Virgin says hoping to fly direct London-Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Virgin says hoping to fly direct London-Shanghai.

text.p: Virgin Group hopes to establish direct flights between the Chinese city of Shanghai and London, Richard Branson, the leader of the diversified British conglomerate, said on Thursday.

"We're also down here to see if we can start to fly direct flights to Shanghai, which obviously is another city that is up and thriving and that doesn't enjoy the pleasures of direct service to London, and we feel that that's something we'd like to be able to offer," Branson said in an interview with the radio arm of Radio Television Hong Kong.
Shanghai's continuing transformation into a cosmopolitan commercial centre could be speeded up through more direct links with major international centres such as London, he added.

"Shanghai is a city that is up and coming and thriving and cut off from the outside world somewhat, mainly because of lack of direct airline services. Once it starts getting more direct airline services from the rest of the world it will be transformed even more than it already has been," Branson said.

Virgin is also considering setting up a new regional carrier to fly some of the shorter routes throughout Asia and the Pacific Rim, but difficulty with permits suggests it would have to be based outside Hong Kong, Branson said.
"I think it'd be quite tough to get the permissions, particularly out of Hong Kong," he said.

"I think we'd have to go somewhere like Singapore who's got a much freer, open market, whereas Hong Kong is very protective of Cathay (Pacific Airways Ltd) and its local carriers and doesn't like to see competition, which is quite strange since it's the city of competition."
Consumers, prices and quality benefit from competition and Virgin will hold discussions with Hong Kong authorities regardless of the anticipated obstacles, he said.
"Airfares between Hong Kong and China, if you compare them with airfares in Europe now, are very, very high," Branson said.

"I think governments are often very mistaken in protecting their flag carriers at the expense of the travelling public, at the expense of tourism, at the expense of the business houses, at the expense of freight, and hopefully that will change in time," he said.
Branson also said Virgin Atlantic is considering increasing the size of its planes servicing the route between Hong Kong and London, which was successfully established two years ago.
